title: Demo tenant API key rotation + least-privilege scopes (with auditability)
creator: Markus Klein
content:
## Context
The demo tenant is used by AEs/SEs for live demos and internal dry runs. Historically the demo org used a small number of long-lived API keys shared in ad-hoc ways. This has caused:
- Key leakage risk (screenshares, copy/paste into docs, overbroad access)
- Slow recovery when a key is suspected compromised (manual revocation + re-seeding)
- Demo instability due to scope mismatches (keys accidentally lack permissions mid-demo)
- Weak audit trails for: who created/rotated a key, when, and what was used during demos

This ticket delivers: scoped keys (least privilege), a repeatable rotation workflow, and auditability sufficient for internal security guidance.

## Goals
1) Least-privilege API keys for demo workflows (SE live demo, synthetic traffic generator, reset automation) with explicit scopes and guardrails.
2) Rotation workflow that takes minutes and is safe to run before major demo days.
3) Auditability: creation, last-used, scope changes, rotation events, and revocations captured in audit logs.
4) Reduce operational footguns: prevent accidental usage of demo keys against non-demo tenants; prevent accidental creation of broad keys.

## Non-goals
- End-user SSO/SAML flows (covered elsewhere; this is demo tenant ops)
- Full secrets management overhaul across the company
- Building a brand-new auth system; this should leverage existing control plane capabilities.

## Proposed key model (scopes + personas)
We will standardize on three key types for demo tenant. Naming convention is enforced by tooling for discoverability:
- `demo-se-live-<initials>-<yyyymmdd>`: For SE live demos; can call inference endpoints + read Console resources needed during the walkthrough.
- `demo-synth-traffic-<region>-<yyyymmdd>`: For the synthetic traffic generator job; only able to hit a narrow set of demo routes.
- `demo-reset-automation-<yyyymmdd>`: For reset + seeding automation; can manage demo projects/routes/keys within demo org only.

Minimum scopes (control-plane terms; exact strings below are implementation-defined and documented in runbooks):
- Live demo key:
  - Inference: chat completions, embeddings, rerank, streaming
  - Console read: usage dashboards, traces, rollouts view (read-only)
  - NO: org admin, billing write, key creation, user management

- Synthetic traffic key:
  - Inference only, limited to allowlisted demo routes/projects
  - Rate-limited for safety
  - NO: console, admin, key creation

- Reset automation key:
  - Project/route CRUD limited to demo org
  - Key rotation actions limited to demo org
  - NO: inference calls (optional; allowed only if reset workflow verifies via a dedicated healthcheck key)

## Implementation plan
### 1) Add/verify fine-grained scopes for demo workflows
- Validate existing scope granularity supports the above separation.
- Where missing, add new scope flags (or map to existing ones) and update authorization checks.
- Ensure Console read-only access can be granted without any write/admin privileges.

### 2) Enforce demo-org boundary in tooling
- Demo keys must be bound to `org_id=demo` and rejected if used against other orgs/tenants.
- Reset and provisioning commands must include environment guards:
  - require `--org demo` and fail closed if mismatch
  - require explicit `--i-understand-this-resets-demo` prompt or a CI-only bypass token

### 3) Rotation workflow
- Add a helper in internal CLI: `rdwd demo keys rotate`
  - Creates new keys for each key type (live/synth/reset) with correct scopes
  - Writes key IDs (not secrets) to a rotation report
  - Supports staged rollout: create new keys, update jobs/config, then revoke old keys
  - Validates that the synthetic traffic generator has successfully ingested data post-rotation
- Document runbook steps and expected timings.

### 4) Auditability
- Ensure audit log events include:
  - `api_key.created` (actor, key_id, org_id, scopes, label)
  - `api_key.revoked`
  - `api_key.rotated` (old_key_id -> new_key_id)
  - `api_key.used` or `auth.token_issued` (key_id, endpoint family, project_id) with sampling if needed
- Add “last used at” to key listing for the demo org to help detect stale keys.

### 5) Rollout
- Start with demo tenant only; feature-flag any new auth logic to avoid impacting production customers.
- Dry run rotation during internal demo practice; then schedule rotation cadence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Live demo can be run end-to-end using a key that cannot create keys, cannot modify org settings, and cannot touch billing settings.
- [x] Synthetic traffic job runs with a key that can only hit allowlisted routes/projects.
- [x] Reset automation runs with a key that can only operate within demo org and cannot affect other tenants.
- [x] One-command rotation produces new keys and revokes old ones with a clear report.
- [x] Audit logs show key creation + revocation + rotation and are searchable by key_id.
- [x] “Last used” is visible (or accessible) for demo keys for hygiene.

## Open questions
- Do we require per-SE unique live keys (preferred) vs a shared live key (discouraged)?
  - Decision: per-SE unique keys for anyone running external demos; shared key permitted only for internal dry runs, rotated weekly.
- Should we store demo key secrets in a vault product?
  - Decision: for now, distribute via the internal key portal + short-lived retrieval window; no secrets in docs or Slack.

## Security review notes
- Reviewed with: Marcus Lin + Naomi Feldman
- Key sharing rules: never post full key material in Slack; only key IDs and links to internal portal.
- Demo recordings/screenshares: OK, but avoid showing the key value; use pre-copied env vars.

## Links
- Related PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28577-scope-api-keys-for-demo-least-privilege.json
- Related work:
  - ENG-4821 Demo tenant provisioning automation
  - ENG-4862 One-command demo reset + health check
  - ENG-4879 Demo environment observability/alerts (audit log surfacing)

## Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Scope too restrictive breaks a live demo path.
  - Mitigation: Add a pre-demo healthcheck that validates permissions (list dashboards, run a short streaming call).
- Risk: Rotation breaks synthetic traffic generator and dashboards go empty.
  - Mitigation: CLI rotation validates ingestion and alerts #demo-oncall if missing after N minutes.
- Risk: People keep old keys.
  - Mitigation: Set max TTL for demo keys and rotate automatically; revoke older than 14 days.

## Updates
### 2025-11-01 (Ethan Park)
Drafted scope matrix and validated we can separate Console read-only permissions from admin. Noted that existing `usage:read` implicitly allowed export in one path—flagged for tightening.

### 2025-11-07 (Markus Klein)
Field feedback: SEs keep asking for a “single key that just works.” Strong preference from security is per-person live keys + a stable rotation workflow. Agreed.

### 2025-11-12 (Ethan Park)
Implemented allowlist restriction for synth traffic key by (project_id, route_id) pair. Added rate limits at the key level to prevent accidental flood during parallel demos.

### 2025-11-18 (Marcus Lin)
Security review: approved direction. Requested that audit logs include `scope_hash` and that rotation emits explicit `api_key.rotated` events (not just create + revoke) to simplify investigations.

### 2025-11-22 (Ethan Park)
CLI `rdwd demo keys rotate` ready behind feature flag. Added environment guardrails; fails closed if org != demo. Added rotation report output (key IDs only).

### 2025-12-02 (Markus Klein)
Dry run rotation during internal demo runthrough. Success. Found one missing permission needed for rollouts view in Console; added `rollouts:read` to live key template. Updated talk track prep checklist to include the key permissions healthcheck.

### 2025-12-04 (Ethan Park)
Shipped + enabled for demo tenant. Old shared keys revoked. Documented rotation cadence (every 14 days, or immediately after any suspected exposure). Ticket complete.

## Notes for SEs
- If a demo key stops working mid-call: run `rdwd demo healthcheck --keys` and switch to the backup per-SE key from the internal key portal.
- If dashboards are empty after rotation: verify synth traffic job uses the new `demo-synth-traffic-*` key and check ingestion status; do not broaden scopes as a workaround.
